entries.title: Annual roof inspection
entries.description: Inspect for damage, wear, and potential leaks.

entries.title: Check for damaged shingles
entries.description: Roofer walks the roof looking for missing, curled, or cracked shingles. Part of the annual inspection or a dedicated post-storm visit.
entries.notes: Also after major storms

entries.title: Clean gutters and downspouts
entries.description: Roofer or gutter service clears debris and verifies downspouts drain away from the foundation.
entries.notes: Spring and fall

entries.title: Inspect flashing around chimney/vents
entries.description: Roofer verifies flashing around chimneys, vents, and skylights is intact and properly sealed.

entries.title: Inspect attic ventilation and insulation
entries.description: Check for adequate ventilation, insulation depth, pest damage, and signs of moisture. Critical for ice dam prevention and winter energy efficiency.
entries.notes: Often bundled into the fall handyman visit or roof inspection.

entries.title: Power wash exterior siding
entries.description: Pressure washer soft-washes siding to remove dirt, mildew, and algae buildup.
entries.notes: Semi-annual is right for vinyl in our region. Wood, brick, and fiber-cement homes can stretch this to once a year. Mixed-material homes follow the more frequent cadence wherever vinyl is present.

entries.title: Deck and patio annual service
entries.description: Handyman or deck pro inspects deck boards, railings, and stairs for rot or loose fasteners; spot-seals as needed. Full stain or seal every 2-3 years.
entries.notes: Seal or stain every 2-3 years

entries.title: Exterior paint touch-up walkaround
entries.description: Walk the exterior with the painter or your handyman to identify peeling, chipping, or weathered paint that needs touch-up. Full repaint is every 7-10 years; annual touch-up catches the spots that fail first (south-facing walls, trim around windows, lower clapboards near grade) and extends the full repaint interval significantly.
entries.notes: Best done in late spring after the wood has dried out from winter and before summer heat. Match the existing finish carefully. Eggshell on a satin wall reads as a patch even after a few weeks of weathering. Most painters keep your color formulation on file once you've used them.

entries.title: Deck or fence staining
entries.description: Strip, sand, and re-stain or seal wood deck and fencing. Annual cleaning extends life; staining every 2-3 years preserves the wood structurally.
entries.notes: Best done in late spring after the wood has fully dried out from winter.

entries.title: Exterior painting refresh
entries.description: Full exterior paint refresh. Scraping, priming, and repainting of siding, trim, and exterior features. Major cycle that HNW owners plan and budget for well in advance.
entries.notes: Plan the contract in winter to lock in a slot on the painter's summer schedule.

entries.title: Driveway seal coat
entries.description: Apply asphalt sealer to protect the driveway against UV, water, and oil damage. Extends driveway life significantly over unsealed asphalt.
entries.notes: Early fall while daytime temps are still warm enough for the sealer to cure. About 3 hours DIY for a typical driveway, or book an asphalt service for a no-effort finish.

entries.title: HVAC tune-up (cooling)
entries.description: HVAC tech inspects and services the air conditioning system before summer. Includes refrigerant level check, condenser coil cleaning, capacitor and contactor inspection, blower motor lubrication, condensate drain flush, and a full system performance test under load. Catches small issues before they become a hot-day breakdown.
entries.notes: Book in February or early March. Most HVAC vendors are fully booked by April once the first warm week hits, and you don't want to be calling around the day your AC stops working in July. Most manufacturer warranties require documented annual service to stay valid.

entries.title: HVAC tune-up (heating)
entries.description: HVAC tech inspects and services the heating system before winter. Includes burner inspection and cleaning, heat exchanger check for cracks (carbon monoxide risk), gas valve and pilot test, blower motor service, thermostat calibration, and a full ignition cycle test. Critical safety check for gas-fired systems.
entries.notes: Book in August or early September. The first cold snap floods every HVAC vendor's voicemail and turns a routine $200 tune-up into a 2-week wait. Annual service is required to maintain most manufacturer warranties.

entries.title: Inspect ductwork for leaks
entries.description: HVAC tech runs a duct-leakage test (typically a Duct Blaster pressurization test or a manual smoke-pencil walkthrough) to find air loss in the supply and return ducts. Most homes lose 20–30% of conditioned air to duct leaks. Sealing them recovers that money on every energy bill for the rest of the system's life.
entries.notes: Older homes (pre-2000) and homes with ductwork running through unconditioned spaces (attic, crawl) benefit most. If your second floor is always 5–10°F off the first floor, leaky ducts are the #1 suspect.

entries.title: Inspect mini-split outdoor unit
entries.description: HVAC tech clears leaves and debris from the outdoor condenser, checks refrigerant line insulation for cracks, washes the coil, verifies the disconnect switch and surge protector, and confirms the unit is level on its pad. Mini-splits can lose 10-20% efficiency to a dirty coil alone.
entries.notes: Often bundled into the spring AC tune-up if your HVAC vendor handles both ducted and ductless. Confirm before booking separately.

entries.title: Bleed radiators
entries.description: Boiler tech opens each radiator's bleed valve in turn to release trapped air, then tops off boiler pressure to spec. Trapped air at the top of a radiator means the bottom half can heat fine while the top stays cold. The room never gets warm even though the system runs constantly.
entries.notes: Most boiler owners include this in the annual boiler service visit instead of a separate appointment. No point paying two trip charges. If you've noticed any radiator running cold or only warming halfway, it's worth flagging to the tech.

entries.title: Annual boiler service
entries.description: Boiler tech runs a full combustion analysis, cleans the burners and combustion chamber, inspects the heat exchanger for cracks (carbon monoxide risk), tests the pressure relief valve, verifies exhaust draft and flue integrity, and checks the expansion tank charge. The most consequential heating-system service in the house. A cracked heat exchanger can leak CO into living spaces.
entries.notes: Required for warranty on most boilers. The manufacturer pulls service records when a claim is filed. Schedule in August or early September. Once the first cold snap hits, every boiler tech is booked solid for 2–3 weeks and a routine service turns into an emergency call.

entries.title: Geothermal loop pressure check
entries.description: Geothermal installer verifies ground loop pressure and antifreeze concentration. A drop of more than 5 PSI/year indicates a leak. Could be a pinhole in the ground loop, fittings at the manifold, or the heat pump's internal pressure switch. Catching this early prevents a full system shutdown.
entries.notes: Use the original installer if possible. Geothermal is specialized. Most general HVAC techs don't have the loop testing equipment or the training to diagnose ground-side issues.

entries.title: Air duct cleaning
entries.description: Professional cleaning of the full supply and return ductwork. Removes dust, allergens, and debris. Separate from the annual HVAC tune-up.
entries.notes: HNW indoor air quality priority. Best done when HVAC is not in heavy use.

entries.title: Flush HVAC condensate drain line
entries.description: Pour a cup of distilled white vinegar down the condensate drain access tee to clear algae and biofilm. Prevents the summer clog that trips the float switch and leaks water into the pan.
entries.notes: Often bundled into the spring cooling tune-up. DIY: locate the white PVC pipe with a threaded cap near the indoor air handler, unscrew the cap, pour vinegar.

entries.title: Drain cleaning
entries.description: Plumber runs a power auger or hydro-jet through the main waste line to clear accumulated grease, soap scum, hair, and root intrusion before it becomes a backup. Includes a camera scope on the cleanout if any line shows resistance. Older homes with cast-iron or clay laterals benefit most.
entries.notes: Houses with mature trees out front are highest-risk for root intrusion. If you've had a slow drain in any fixture in the last 6 months, prioritize this. The same root that's slowing one drain will eventually back up the whole house.

entries.title: Test sump pump battery backup
entries.description: Unplug the primary sump pump to verify the battery backup engages and can move water. Most backup batteries last 5-7 years. If it doesn't hold charge, replace before spring rains.
entries.notes: About 10 minutes DIY. Test in spring before wet season and in fall before storm season.

entries.title: Flush water heater
entries.description: Plumber drains and flushes sediment from the tank, tests the T&P relief valve, and inspects the sacrificial anode rod (replace if more than 50% depleted). Standard package keeps the tank free of buildup that drives up gas/electric usage and shortens lifespan.
entries.notes: Anode rod inspection is part of the standard flush. Pros pull and inspect every visit and replace when depleted past ~50%. The replacement requires a partial drain plus a 1-1/16" socket and breaker bar, both of which the plumber already has on the truck.

entries.title: Test T&P relief valve
entries.description: Plumber tests the temperature and pressure relief valve for proper operation. Typically bundled with the annual water heater flush.
entries.notes: Safety-critical valve check

entries.title: Descale tankless heater
entries.description: Plumber flushes a vinegar or commercial descaler solution through the tankless unit's heat exchanger for 30–45 minutes, then rinses with fresh water. Removes mineral scale that builds up on the heat exchanger plates and slowly chokes flow rate, drives up gas/electric usage, and shortens lifespan. Critical for warranty.
entries.notes: Hard water areas (well water + most municipal water in the Northeast) may need every 6 months. If you notice the unit cycling more often or hot water taking longer to arrive, you're already overdue. Most manufacturer warranties require documented annual descaling.

entries.title: Septic tank pumping
entries.description: Pumping of septic tank to remove accumulated solids.
entries.notes: Two-year default for a typical 4-person household with a 1,000-gallon tank. Larger households (6+) should pump annually; small households (1-2 people) with larger tanks can stretch to 3 years. Inspector will tell you the actual sludge level on each visit and recalibrate.

entries.title: Inspect septic baffles
entries.description: Septic service inspects baffles during pumping to ensure they're intact.
entries.notes: Done during pumping

entries.title: Test water quality
entries.description: Certified lab tests a sample for total coliform bacteria, E. coli, nitrates, nitrites, lead, and pH. Iron, manganese, hardness, and arsenic add-on panels are recommended in the Northeast and parts of the Midwest where geology drives elevated levels. Results take 5–10 business days.
entries.notes: Test in spring after the snowmelt and seasonal water-table shifts have moved through. Test sooner if you notice taste, odor, or color changes. Those are the canary signs of a contamination event. State health departments often offer free or subsidized testing for private wells.

entries.title: Well system inspection
entries.description: Well service comprehensively inspects the submersible pump, well casing integrity, pressure tank pre-charge and bladder, pressure switch and gauge, electrical connections at the well head, and total water output (gallons per minute). Catches a failing pump before it dies on a Saturday night.
entries.notes: Pump replacement is $1,500–$3,500. Annual inspection catches the early warning signs (cycling more often, lower flow, casing seal issues) and lets you plan the replacement on your schedule rather than during an emergency.

entries.title: Replace smoke detectors
entries.description: Electrician or handyman replaces smoke detectors that have passed their 10-year lifespan. Detectors have a manufacture date printed on the back. After 10 years the sensor degrades and false-positive / false-negative rates climb sharply. This is one of the few maintenance items where the timing isn't optional.
entries.notes: If you have hardwired/interconnected detectors, replace them all at once with the same model. Mixing brands or sensor types in an interconnected system can cause false alarms. Check the manufacture date on every detector while up there; some homes have a mix of newer and older units.

entries.title: Inspect electrical panel
entries.description: Electrician opens the main breaker panel to check for signs of wear: burned or discolored bus bars, loose terminations, corrosion, water staining, and breakers that feel warm to the touch under load. Catches the early warning signs of a panel that's nearing end-of-life or has a high-current connection slowly arcing.
entries.notes: Federal Pacific (FPE), Zinsco, and Sylvania-Challenger panels are known fire risks. If you have one and haven't replaced it, inspection is critical and a panel swap ($2K–$4K) should be on the radar. Most insurance companies will discount your premium after a panel upgrade.

entries.title: EV charger inspection
entries.description: Electrician inspects the EV charging station hardware, dedicated circuit and breaker, terminations at the charger and the panel, and the charging cable for wear or heat signatures. Higher-amperage L2 installs (40A / 50A circuits) draw more current for longer durations than typical residential loads. A slowly-loosening connection runs hot for months before it fails.
entries.notes: If your charger is in an unconditioned garage or outdoors, check the housing for rodent damage and water intrusion at the same time. Some manufacturer warranties require documented annual inspection. Ask before you buy if you're shopping a new install.

entries.templateKey: Electrical:IR scan of main electrical panel
entries.title: IR scan of main electrical panel
entries.description: Electrician uses a thermal imaging camera to identify loose breaker connections and pre-arc heat signatures before they fail. Non-invasive ~30 minute visit; pairs with the 3-year visual inspection.
entries.notes: Ask for thermal images to be included in the service report for your home records.

entries.title: Heat cable inspection
entries.description: Electrician verifies heat trace cables on gutters, roof edges, or exposed pipes are intact, properly thermostat-controlled, and drawing the right amperage. Replace damaged sections before snowfall.
entries.notes: Pair with the heating tune-up or fall roof inspection so the electrician can see the cable routing.

entries.title: Outdoor lighting system service
entries.description: Lighting tech inspects every fixture, re-aims lamps, replaces bulbs, checks transformer output, and reseals any failed connections. Catches the dim-spot-here / dark-spot-there drift that accumulates over a year.
entries.notes: Best done in early spring before you're outside at night enjoying the landscape.

entries.title: Fire extinguisher annual check
entries.description: Walk to every extinguisher, verify the pressure gauge is in the green, the tamper seal is intact, and the inspection tag is signed for the current year. Replace any unit past its 12-year service life.
entries.notes: Log inspection dates on the tag so you can track service history. Commercial recharge runs $25-75 per extinguisher.

entries.title: Annual chimney sweep
entries.description: Chimney sweep cleans and inspects the chimney and flue. Critical for wood-burning fireplaces to prevent creosote buildup and chimney fires.
entries.notes: Schedule before first use each season. Each chimney is swept separately. If you have multiple flues, mention it so the sweep allocates the right amount of time.

entries.title: Inspect chimney cap and crown
entries.description: Roofer or mason inspects the chimney cap, crown, and mortar joints from the roof. Catches animal entry points, damaged screens, and early cracks in the crown before water infiltration damages the flue liner.
entries.notes: Often folded into the annual roof inspection or a chimney-sweep visit.

entries.title: Annual gas fireplace service
entries.description: Gas tech inspects burner, pilot light, gas connections, thermopile/thermocouple, and logs. Distinct from a sweep. Gas fireplaces don't need creosote cleaning but they do need annual gas-side service.
entries.notes: Typically the same HVAC tech who handles your gas furnace can do this, or a specialty gas fireplace service.

entries.title: Schedule exterior window re-caulking
entries.description: Painter or handyman scrapes out cracked or pulling-away exterior caulk around every window and door, applies fresh exterior-grade urethane or polyurethane sealant, and tools the bead clean. Failed exterior caulk is the #1 entry point for water damage to wall framing. Catching it early prevents wood rot and the $5K+ repair that follows.
entries.notes: Look for caulk that's pulled away from the trim, has hairline cracks, or has yellowed (older silicone). Schedule before fall rains so the new bead has dry weather to skin over before winter freeze-thaw cycles stress it. Often paired with a touch-up paint visit in the same trip.

entries.title: Test garage door auto-reverse
entries.description: Tech confirms the auto-reverse safety feature works by placing an object in the door path. Bundled with the annual tune-up.
entries.notes: Modern openers self-monitor between visits.

siblings: Garage Door:Lubricate garage door tracks and hardware

entries.templateKey: Garage Door:Lubricate garage door tracks and hardware
entries.title: Lubricate garage door tracks and hardware
entries.description: Tech applies silicone lubricant to tracks, rollers, hinges, and springs. Part of the annual tune-up.

entries.title: Annual garage door tune-up
entries.description: Inspection of springs, cables, rollers, and opener.
entries.notes: Never attempt spring repair yourself

siblings: Garage Door:Lubricate garage door tracks and hardware

entries.title: Mulch garden beds
entries.description: Landscaper adds 2-3 inches of fresh mulch to garden beds to retain moisture and suppress weeds.

entries.title: Prune shrubs and hedges
entries.description: Landscaper trims overgrown shrubs and hedges for health and appearance. Spring and fall.

entries.title: Fertilize natural lawn
entries.description: Landscaper applies seasonal fertilizer appropriate for grass type and season. Three rounds per year keeps roots strong and color deep.

entries.title: Core aerate natural lawn
entries.description: Landscaper pulls soil plugs to reduce compaction and let water and nutrients reach roots. Paired with fall overseeding.

entries.title: Overseed bare patches
entries.description: Landscaper spreads fresh seed in thin or bare areas. Best paired with fall aeration so seed-to-soil contact is maximized.
entries.notes: Cool-season grasses seed best in early fall

entries.title: Pre-emergent weed control
entries.description: Landscaper applies pre-emergent herbicide before crabgrass and other weeds germinate.
entries.notes: Timed to soil temps in the low 50s. Usually mid-March to mid-April in {state}

entries.title: Dethatch lawn
entries.description: Landscaper uses a power rake or thatching attachment to remove built-up thatch. Skipped when thatch is under 1/2".

entries.templateKey: Landscaping:Soil pH test and lime application
entries.title: Soil pH test and lime application
entries.description: Landscaper pulls soil core samples from a few representative spots, runs a pH test, and applies dolomitic or calcitic lime in measured amounts to bring acidic soil back to 6.0–7.0 where cool-season grasses thrive. Acidic soil locks out nutrients even when you're fertilizing. Without correcting pH first, the fertilizer is wasted money.
entries.notes: Lime needs 3–6 months to fully react with soil, so fall application gives it the winter to do its work before spring growth. Northeast soils are naturally acidic from rainfall; if you've never tested, you're almost certainly low.

entries.title: Fall leaf cleanup
entries.description: Landscaping crew clears leaves from the lawn and garden beds. Letting them sit through winter smothers the grass and invites snow mold.

entries.title: Top up turf infill
entries.description: Turf specialist refreshes the rubber or silica sand infill that holds the synthetic fibers upright. Infill migrates over time from rain runoff, foot traffic, and seasonal grooming. Without it, fibers mat down and the turf looks worn long before its 12–15 year design life.
entries.notes: Most synthetic-turf vendors offer this as part of an annual service plan. If you've noticed footprints staying visible after walking on the turf, you're already overdue.

entries.title: Power rake and groom turf
entries.description: Turf specialist runs a power rake or groomer across the surface to lift matted fibers, redistribute migrated infill, and remove debris that's worked into the pile. Keeps the turf looking new and bouncy through year 15+ instead of going flat at year 5.
entries.notes: Twice-a-year is the manufacturer recommendation for most premium turf. Spring grooming opens up the pile after winter compaction; fall grooming clears leaves and acorns before they break down into organic matter (which then feeds weed growth between blades).

entries.title: Deep clean synthetic turf
entries.description: Turf cleaning service uses a power groomer + extraction vacuum to pull embedded debris, pollen, dust, and pet residue out of the infill layer. Goes deeper than the annual top-up + grooming visit. Extends usable turf life by 3–5 years and resets the look to near-new for HNW homeowners who notice surface fade.
entries.notes: Schedule for early spring before the heaviest pollen weeks. That way the infill is clean before the year's accumulation starts. If you have dogs or kids using the turf heavily, consider every year rather than every two.

entries.title: Outdoor lighting service
entries.description: Lighting specialist checks the low-voltage transformer, replaces failed LEDs, adjusts timers and photocells, inspects and cleans fixtures, and re-aims uplights after any landscape changes.
entries.notes: HNW landscape lighting investment warrants a dedicated vendor.

entries.title: Arborist tree health inspection
entries.description: Certified arborist inspects mature trees for disease, structural weakness, and storm risk. Liability protection. Falling tree damage is often excluded from home insurance if due to visible neglect.
entries.notes: Best done in early fall before leaf-out obscures the structural picture.

entries.title: Pressure wash patio and walkways
entries.description: Pressure wash stone, paver, and concrete hardscape surfaces to clear winter grime, mildew, and algae. Use a fan tip and avoid stripping joint sand.
entries.notes: About 2 hours DIY. Pros finish faster and catch what a homeowner would miss.

entries.title: Top up joint sand in pavers
entries.description: Sweep polymeric joint sand into paver gaps where it has washed out. Mist lightly to set the polymer. Prevents weed germination and keeps pavers locked.
entries.notes: About 1 hour DIY.

entries.title: Treat weeds between pavers
entries.description: Spot-treat weeds growing between pavers and along hardscape edges. Pull large clumps by hand first, then apply a targeted herbicide or boiling water.
entries.notes: About 30 minutes DIY.

entries.title: Check hardscape drainage and grading
entries.description: Walk hardscape edges after a rain to confirm water is moving away from the house. Look for sunken pavers, ponding, and drainage swales that have silted in.
entries.notes: About 30 minutes DIY. A landscaping contractor will catch grading issues that aren't obvious to a homeowner.

entries.title: Winterize irrigation system
entries.description: Irrigation tech connects an air compressor to the system, isolates each zone in turn, and blows compressed air through the lines until water stops emerging from the heads. Drains the backflow preventer and shuts the main supply at the curb stop. A single skipped year on a freeze-prone climate can split mainlines underground.
entries.notes: Must be done before the first hard freeze. Once water freezes inside a head or valve, it cracks the brass. And you don't find out until spring startup when the system pressurizes and the leaks reveal themselves. In the Northeast, target mid-October.

entries.title: Spring startup irrigation
entries.description: Irrigation service gradually pressurizes the system zone by zone, watching for unexpected geysers from cracked heads or split lines that froze over winter. Adjusts spray patterns for fresh landscape growth, replaces broken heads, and tests the rain sensor and controller. Sets the seasonal watering schedule.
entries.notes: Schedule for after the last hard freeze (mid-April in the Northeast, earlier south). If your vendor pressurizes before the ground thaws fully you risk a burst on a still-frozen line.

entries.title: Backflow preventer test
entries.description: Licensed backflow tester verifies the assembly prevents irrigation water from contaminating the potable supply. Legally required annually in most municipalities.
entries.notes: Your water utility may send an annual reminder. Many irrigation services include the test with spring startup.

entries.title: Pool opening service
entries.description: Pool service removes the cover, starts up equipment, balances chemicals, and inspects.

entries.title: Pool closing and winterization
entries.description: Pool service handles chemical treatment, lowers water level, blows out lines, and installs cover.

entries.title: Inspect pool equipment
entries.description: Pool service checks pump, heater, filter, and automation for proper operation during opening.
entries.notes: Done during opening

entries.title: Pool heater service
entries.description: Pool heater specialist services the heater. Gas heaters get a combustion check, burner cleaning, and pilot/igniter inspection; heat pumps get refrigerant, coil, and defrost-cycle verification. Annual service doubles heater lifespan.
entries.notes: Folded into the Pool Opening Service bundle so the heater is ready for the first cool spring night.

entries.title: Drain and refill hot tub
entries.description: Drain the tub completely, wipe the shell, and refill with fresh water. Can be DIY or scheduled with a spa service.
entries.notes: Detached hot tubs only. If your spa shares water with the pool (spillover / attached configuration), skip this. The pool service handles drain and refill via the pool seasonal close. Plan 2-3 hours for the standalone drain + refill cycle.

entries.templateKey: Pool/Spa:Inspect hot tub cover and jets
entries.title: Inspect hot tub cover and jets
entries.description: Check the cover for cracks, waterlogging (lift one corner. If it's noticeably heavier than the opposite corner, the foam is saturated), and torn vinyl. Test each jet for pressure and verify the aim hasn't drifted. Inspect the cover lifter mechanism if equipped.
entries.notes: Detached hot tubs only — attached spillover spas don't have removable covers in this sense, and their jet inspection rolls into the pool opening visit. A waterlogged cover loses 20–40% of its insulation value, costing $30–$60/month in extra heating during cool months. Replacement covers run $300–$500. Pays for itself in 6–12 months. Soaked covers also start to mold inside, which is gross to rest your face on.

entries.title: Pool safety fence inspection
entries.description: Inspect the pool safety fence and gate: self-closing mechanism, latch height (at least 54"), no gaps greater than 4", and any damaged mesh or posts. Required by law in CT and many HNW municipalities.
entries.notes: Pair with pool opening. Fence service can handle if the gate needs adjustment.

entries.title: Clean dryer vent duct
entries.description: Dryer vent service cleans the full vent duct run. Lint accumulation is the leading cause of dryer fires after cooking equipment.
entries.notes: Often folded into the fall handyman visit.

entries.title: Replace refrigerator water filter
entries.description: Haven adds this to your handyman punch list every six months. Drop a fresh filter on the counter and the swap takes 30 seconds. No handyman? Most fridge manufacturers offer a subscription that ships your filter at the right interval.
entries.notes: Filter SKU varies by fridge model. Pull the model number from the inside-door sticker and search the manufacturer site, or tap your refrigerator in the equipment catalog for a direct reorder link.

entries.title: Built-in grill service
entries.description: Grill specialist deep-cleans burners, grates, and the firebox; runs a gas-line pressure test; inspects the igniter and thermocouples; replaces worn parts. Protects the outdoor kitchen investment and keeps gas connections safe.
entries.notes: Schedule before grilling season starts.

entries.title: Termite inspection
entries.description: Pest control inspector walks the perimeter looking for mud tubes, swarmer wings near windows, frass, and damaged wood. Probes accessible sills, joists, and structural members in the basement / crawl space. Pulls back mulch and inspects siding contact points. The visible signs are usually small and easy to miss until they're catastrophic.
entries.notes: Spring is termite swarming season. The easiest time to spot active colonies. Required to maintain most home warranties. If the inspector finds activity, treatment runs $1,500–$5,000 depending on severity, but skipping the inspection can mean a $30K+ structural repair down the line.

entries.title: Change generator oil
entries.description: Generator tech drains and replaces oil per manufacturer schedule. Standby generators run hot and the oil drain is awkward.
entries.notes: Every 200 hours or annually

entries.title: Replace spark plugs
entries.description: Replace spark plugs per manufacturer recommendations. Usually done as part of annual service.

entries.title: Annual generator service
entries.description: Full service including all fluids, filters, and electrical check.
entries.notes: Before winter storm season

entries.title: Test automatic transfer switch
entries.description: Test of transfer switch operation during annual service.

entries.title: Annual security system check
entries.description: Alarm company walk-tests each sensor, confirms panel connectivity, and replaces sensor batteries. Monitored systems self-test between visits. This is the annual confirmation that everything is still registering.

entries.title: Replace sensor batteries
entries.description: Alarm tech replaces batteries in door/window sensors and motion detectors. Bundled with the annual walk-test.

entries.title: Solar panel cleaning
entries.description: Roof-trained crew cleans accumulated pollen, dust, bird droppings, and pine sap off the array using deionized water and soft brushes. Avoids harsh detergents and pressure-washing that can strip the anti-reflective coating. Output gain after a thorough cleaning is typically 5–15% on heavily soiled panels.
entries.notes: Output drops gradually so it's hard to notice from monthly bills alone. But a year of accumulated soiling can cost $200–$500 in lost generation depending on system size. Spring is ideal (after pollen settles, before peak production months).

entries.title: Solar system inspection
entries.description: Solar tech checks panel integrity (microcracks, hot spots, junction box issues), DC and AC wiring at the combiner box and inverter, mounting hardware torque on the rails and roof attachments, and inverter performance against expected output curves. Catches degraded panels before they take down a string and tank production.
entries.notes: Most production warranties require inspection records to honor a claim. If your inverter is approaching 8–10 years old, ask the inspector to flag whether it's nearing replacement age. Inverter failure is the #1 cause of unexpected solar downtime.

entries.title: Check vapor barrier condition
entries.description: Crawl-space or waterproofing pro inspects the plastic vapor barrier for tears, displacement, or gaps.

siblings: Crawl Space:Inspect for mold or mildew

entries.templateKey: Crawl Space:Inspect for mold or mildew
entries.title: Inspect for mold or mildew
entries.description: Pro visually inspects joists, insulation, and walls for mold growth.
entries.notes: Professional remediation if found

entries.title: Check foundation for cracks
entries.description: Pro inspects foundation walls for new or expanding cracks and marks any findings.

siblings: Crawl Space:Inspect for mold or mildew

entries.title: Test smart water leak system
entries.description: Exercise the shutoff valve, test each leak sensor, confirm the app connectivity (Moen Flo, Phyn, etc.). Quick handyman task that lands on the spring visit.

entries.title: Service central vacuum system
entries.description: Empty the canister, replace the bag or filter, inspect the hose and attachments, and clear any wall-port clogs. Easy to overlook. Lands on the fall handyman visit.

entries.title: Verify radon mitigation fan
entries.description: Confirm the mitigation fan reads correctly on its manometer. The fan should run continuously. If the manometer is flat on both sides, the fan has failed and needs replacement.
entries.notes: Lands on the fall handyman visit alongside smoke detector checks.

entries.title: Replace smoke & CO detector batteries
entries.description: Swap batteries in every smoke and CO detector. Modern sealed 10-year detectors don't need this, but most homes still have a mix of battery-powered units that the handyman catches in one visit.

entries.title: Inspect exterior caulking around windows & doors
entries.description: Walk the exterior and check the caulk bead around every window and door. The handyman spot-recaulks any gaps or separations before spring rains.

entries.title: Foundation walkaround: cracks and grading
entries.description: Walk the foundation perimeter. Check for new cracks, signs of efflorescence, and areas where soil has settled and now slopes toward the house.

entries.title: Check washing machine supply hoses
entries.description: Inspect the hot and cold supply hoses behind the washing machine for bulges, cracks, or moisture. Burst hoses are the #1 source of catastrophic laundry-room water damage.

entries.title: Test sump pump function
entries.description: Pour a few gallons of water into the sump pit and confirm the pump kicks on and discharges. Catches pumps that have silently seized over winter.
entries.notes: Distinct from the Phase 62 battery backup test. This one confirms the primary pump still cycles.

entries.title: Test GFCI outlets throughout house
entries.description: Press the TEST button on every GFCI outlet (kitchen, bathrooms, garage, exterior) and confirm it trips and resets. A GFCI that won't trip is a safety failure.

entries.title: Test smoke and CO detector alarms
entries.description: Hold the TEST button on every alarm to confirm the sounder works. Separate from battery swap. This verifies the audio circuit.

entries.title: Replace HVAC filter (cooling season)
entries.description: Swap to a fresh filter heading into cooling season. The handyman stocks the right size for your system so you don't have to remember.

entries.title: Ceiling fan direction switch (summer)
entries.description: Flip ceiling fans to counter-clockwise for downward airflow during cooling season. Reachable units only. The handyman handles the ones requiring a ladder.

entries.title: Reopen exterior faucets post-winter
entries.description: Confirm every exterior faucet reopens without leaks after winter. Split pipes behind the spigot reveal themselves the first time you turn on the hose.

entries.title: Replace smoke & CO detector batteries
entries.description: Fall battery swap. Daylight-saving is the industry's mnemonic. The handyman handles the high-reach units you can't get to safely.

entries.title: Winterize outdoor faucets and hose bibs
entries.description: Shut off interior supply valves to exterior faucets, open the spigots to drain, install insulated covers. A split pipe behind the bib is a $2-5K repair.

entries.title: Drain and store exterior hoses
entries.description: Drain every exterior hose, coil, and store in a garage or shed so they don't crack from freeze-thaw cycles.

entries.title: Inspect weatherstripping pre-heating season
entries.description: Check door and window weatherstripping for gaps, compression, or tears. Replace any compromised sections before the heating bill reflects them.

entries.title: Pre-winter foundation and gutter walkaround
entries.description: Check foundation + gutters before freeze season. Any cracks that need sealing + any gutter hangers that loosened over the summer.

entries.title: Check attic insulation coverage
entries.description: Eye-check the attic. Look for areas where insulation has been compressed, blown aside, or compromised by pests. Snap a photo for later reference.

entries.title: Test smoke and CO detector alarms
entries.description: Fall audio-circuit verification. Press TEST on every alarm. Especially important before the heating system starts producing CO.

entries.title: Replace HVAC filter (heating season)
entries.description: Swap to a fresh filter before the furnace starts running. A loaded filter slows airflow and costs runtime.

entries.title: Ceiling fan direction switch (winter)
entries.description: Flip ceiling fans to clockwise for gentle upward airflow. Pushes warm air pooling at the ceiling back down into the room.

entries.title: Pipe insulation check in unheated spaces
entries.description: Confirm pipe insulation is intact in garages, crawl spaces, attics, and unheated basements. Replace any sections that have fallen away or been chewed on.

entries.title: Interior paint touch-up walkaround
entries.description: Handyman walks the house with a small kit (primer, paint matched to existing finishes, a fine brush) and touches up scuffs, nicks, and baseboard marks. A 90-minute visit keeps a refreshed look without a full repaint.
entries.notes: Bring your touch-up paint kit if you have one. Most handymen can color-match from a sample chip if you don't.

entries.title: Smart home battery sweep
entries.description: Handyman replaces batteries across every smart lock, doorbell camera, smoke/CO detector, motion sensor, and smart home hub. Most HNW homes have 15-30 battery-powered devices. This catches the ones the owner never thinks about until they die.
entries.notes: Pair with the spring or fall handyman visit.

entries.title: Ceiling fan cleaning and balancing
entries.description: Handyman cleans every ceiling fan blade and tests balance (wobble means it's out of spec). High-reach task that accumulates dust for years because no one wants to drag out a ladder. Balanced fans are also quieter.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Drywall patch and paint touch-up visit
entries.title: Drywall patch and paint touch-up visit
entries.description: Bundle the nail pops, scuffs, small dents, and hairline drywall cracks into one visit so the handyman can patch, sand, and spot-paint the obvious lived-in wear all at once.
entries.notes: Great quote-friendly add-on before guests, photos, or listing prep.

entries.title: Door, latch, and hinge tune-up
entries.description: Handyman adjusts sticking interior doors, noisy hinges, misaligned strike plates, loose closers, and dragging thresholds. Small fixes that make the whole house feel maintained.

entries.title: Window screen and hardware repair
entries.description: Replace torn screens, tighten latches, adjust sash hardware, and fix the easy window annoyances that owners tolerate for years.
entries.notes: Especially useful before bug season or when opening the house back up after winter.

entries.title: Interior caulk refresh
entries.description: Re-caulk the obvious failure points in kitchens, mudrooms, and baths before water gets behind trim, counters, or fixtures. Good example of low-drama work that prevents bigger repairs.
entries.notes: Modern silicone caulk holds up for 2-3 years before showing failure points. Annual was overkill for most households. Escalate to a tile setter or plumber if there is movement, active water damage, or fixture replacement hiding underneath.

entries.title: Furniture, playset, or shed assembly
entries.description: Use the handyman for assemblies that are tedious, tool-heavy, or safer with two sets of hands. This keeps the homeowner out of half-finished box chaos.
entries.notes: Good fit for outdoor season starts, playroom upgrades, and storage cleanup.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Fence, gate, and deck repair sweep
entries.title: Fence, gate, and deck repair sweep
entries.description: Tighten hinges, replace a few boards, fix sagging latches, and handle the small exterior repairs that are annoying on their own but perfect when bundled together.
entries.notes: Good seasonal add-on when the handyman is already doing the spring exterior walkthrough.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Patch nail holes and small drywall dings
entries.title: Patch nail holes and small drywall dings
entries.description: Fill, sand, and prime small holes from previous artwork or scuffs. The handyman runs the room with spackle, a putty knife, and a touch-up paint match.
entries.notes: About 5 minutes per hole; bundle multiple rooms into one visit.

entries.title: Touch up scuffed wall paint
entries.description: Match and feather paint into scuffs, kid marks, and high-traffic wear spots. Best on flat or eggshell finishes; satin and semi-gloss often need a full wall.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Patch stuck or sticking interior doors
entries.title: Patch stuck or sticking interior doors
entries.description: Plane the door edge or shim hinges so doors close cleanly. Common after a humid summer or a foundation settle.

entries.title: Repair damaged drywall corner bead
entries.description: Replace dented or bent corner bead and refloat the corner. The repair disappears once the new compound dries and gets a touch-up coat.

entries.title: Spot-paint interior trim and baseboards
entries.description: Touch up scuffs and chips on trim, baseboards, and door casings. The handyman matches sheen and color from your existing paint can.

entries.title: Re-caulk around tubs and tile
entries.description: Strip old caulk along tub-to-tile and tile-to-wall seams, sanitize, and lay a fresh mildew-resistant bead. Prevents water seepage behind the tile.

entries.title: Re-grout small tile sections
entries.description: Remove failing or stained grout from a defined section and re-grout. Sealing afterward extends the life of the new grout.

entries.title: Lubricate squeaky door hinges
entries.description: Apply a dry lubricant or graphite to hinges throughout the house. Quick to do but easy to overlook. Handyman often catches it on a punch-list visit.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Tighten loose stair balusters and handrails
entries.title: Tighten loose stair balusters and handrails
entries.description: Re-secure wobbly stair components. Most fixes are tightening hidden screws or re-gluing where the joinery has loosened.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Wax hardwood floors in high-traffic areas
entries.title: Wax hardwood floors in high-traffic areas
entries.description: Buff and wax sections of hardwood that show wear (entryways, hallways, in front of sinks). Restores sheen without a full refinish.

entries.title: Replace torn window screens
entries.description: Restretch or replace damaged window-screen mesh. The handyman cuts new mesh, secures it with spline, and trims the excess.

entries.title: Replace exterior door weatherstripping
entries.description: Swap weatherstripping that's compressed, torn, or no longer sealing. Prevents drafts and cuts heating/cooling waste at the door.

entries.title: Adjust door strike plates
entries.description: Move or shim strike plates so doors latch cleanly without pushing. Common after seasonal humidity shifts move the door slightly.

entries.title: Lubricate sliding door tracks
entries.description: Vacuum the track, clean the rollers, and apply a silicone lubricant. Restores smooth glide on patio doors and pocket doors.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Re-key a deadbolt or door knob
entries.title: Re-key a deadbolt or door knob
entries.description: Replace the lock cylinder pins so old keys no longer work. Common after move-in, contractor handoff, or lost keys.
entries.notes: A locksmith is faster for matched key sets across multiple doors.

entries.title: Replace exterior door bottom sweep
entries.description: Swap the sweep on the bottom of an exterior door. Restores the seal against the threshold and stops light or draft at the floor.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Tighten loose door handles and knockers
entries.title: Tighten loose door handles and knockers
entries.description: Re-secure door handles, knockers, and other exterior hardware that's worked loose over time.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Repair or replace casement window cranks
entries.title: Repair or replace casement window cranks
entries.description: Swap a casement crank that's stripped, broken, or no longer engaging the operator. Restores full open/close range.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Reseal a stuck or sticking window
entries.title: Reseal a stuck or sticking window
entries.description: Free a window that's painted shut or swollen, clean the channel, and lubricate. Often the fix is a utility knife and silicone spray.

entries.title: Swap a single light fixture
entries.description: Replace a sconce, flush mount, or pendant. The handyman handles the wiring, mounting, and bulb test.

entries.title: Replace a ceiling fan
entries.description: Remove the existing fan and install a replacement. Includes balancing the new blades and confirming the mounting box is rated for fans.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Replace a bathroom or vanity light fixture
entries.title: Replace a bathroom or vanity light fixture
entries.description: Swap a vanity bar or sconce. The handyman matches the existing junction box footprint and confirms ground continuity.

entries.title: Install USB-equipped outlets
entries.description: Replace existing duplex outlets with USB-A or USB-C outlets in nightstands, kitchen counters, or desks. Handles the load calc to confirm the circuit can support it.

entries.title: Install or replace dimmer switches
entries.description: Swap a single-pole or three-way switch with a dimmer. The handyman confirms compatibility with LED loads to prevent flicker.

entries.title: Replace a basic thermostat
entries.description: Swap a non-line-voltage thermostat. The handyman confirms wiring (R/C/W/Y/G) and verifies heating and cooling commands.

entries.title: Install smart light switches
entries.description: Swap dumb single-pole or three-way switches for smart equivalents (Lutron Caséta, Leviton Decora, Kasa). The handyman handles the neutral check and app pairing.
entries.notes: Often paired with new dimmer install; bundle multiple rooms into one visit.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Replace a porch or pendant fixture
entries.title: Replace a porch or pendant fixture
entries.description: Swap an exterior sconce, post lantern, or front-porch pendant. Includes a check for adequate weather sealing on the housing.

entries.title: Install a video doorbell
entries.description: Mount and configure a battery- or wired-doorbell camera. Includes connecting to home Wi-Fi and verifying the chime or app feed.

entries.title: Replace cabinet door hinges
entries.description: Swap matching hinges that have rusted, sagged, or stripped out. The handyman matches cup size and overlay for a clean fit.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Adjust cabinet doors so they close evenly
entries.title: Adjust cabinet doors so they close evenly
entries.description: Tighten or shim cabinet doors that have drifted out of alignment. Quick adjustment screws on European hinges fix most cases.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Add soft-close adapters to cabinet doors
entries.title: Add soft-close adapters to cabinet doors
entries.description: Retrofit existing cabinet doors with soft-close hinge adapters or pads. Quiets slamming and protects the cabinet edges.

entries.title: Replace drawer slides
entries.description: Swap broken or sagging slides for full-extension or soft-close replacements. The handyman matches mount type (side, bottom, undermount).

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Repair a sagging or broken cabinet door
entries.title: Repair a sagging or broken cabinet door
entries.description: Re-glue a separated joint, replace a cracked panel, or shim a hinge plate. Restores the door without a full replacement.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Tighten loose cabinet pulls and knobs
entries.title: Tighten loose cabinet pulls and knobs
entries.description: Snug up hardware throughout the kitchen, bath, and built-ins. Often paired with a hinge tune-up on the same visit.

entries.title: Replace damaged shelf supports
entries.description: Swap stripped or broken shelf pins and clips. The handyman confirms the new pin matches the shelf-hole diameter.

entries.title: Replace a toilet seat
entries.description: Swap a worn, stained, or wobbly toilet seat. The handyman matches round vs. elongated and confirms hardware torque.

entries.title: Swap a shower head
entries.description: Replace an existing shower head with a new fixture (rain, handheld, dual). Includes pipe-thread sealing to prevent leaks.

entries.title: Clean and replace faucet aerators
entries.description: Unscrew aerators on bathroom and kitchen faucets, soak in vinegar to dissolve mineral build-up, and reinstall (or replace if corroded).
entries.notes: Cheap fix that often restores full pressure on a faucet that feels weak.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Re-caulk perimeter of tub or shower
entries.title: Re-caulk perimeter of tub or shower
entries.description: Cut out failing caulk along the tub-tile or pan-wall seam, sanitize, and lay a fresh mildew-resistant bead. Stops water from getting behind the surround.

entries.title: Clean and reseal shower grout
entries.description: Scrub stained or mildewed grout, neutralize with a grout cleaner, and apply a penetrating sealer. Extends the life of the existing grout for years.

entries.title: Replace bathroom exhaust fan grille
entries.description: Swap a stained, yellowed, or noisy grille on a bath fan. Includes vacuuming the housing while the cover is off.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Replace a toilet flapper or fill valve
entries.title: Replace a toilet flapper or fill valve
entries.description: Swap the rubber flapper, fill valve, or both on a toilet that runs continuously or won't fully fill. Most fixes use a universal kit.

entries.title: Stabilize a rocking toilet
entries.description: Reseat the toilet on a fresh wax ring and shim the base so it's level. Stops the rocking that breaks the wax seal and starts a slow leak.

entries.title: Reset a stuck garbage disposal
entries.description: Use the underside reset button and the manual hex key to free a jammed disposal. Quick fix when the disposal hums but won't spin.

entries.title: Replace kitchen faucet aerator
entries.description: Unscrew the kitchen aerator, descale or replace, and reinstall. Restores full flow on a faucet that's lost pressure.

entries.title: Clean range hood grease filters
entries.description: Remove the metal mesh filters and run them through the dishwasher or soak in degreaser. Restores hood efficiency and cuts fire risk.
entries.notes: Replace charcoal filters annually if your hood recirculates instead of vents outside.

entries.title: Replace refrigerator door gasket
entries.description: Swap a torn or compressed door seal so the fridge holds temperature. Compressor cycles less; ice and frost stop forming around the door.

entries.title: Tighten a loose kitchen sink
entries.description: Re-secure a sink that's pulled away from the countertop or shifted in the cutout. Stops water from running behind the cabinet.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Replace a worn dish soap or instant-hot pump
entries.title: Replace a worn dish soap or instant-hot pump
entries.description: Swap a dish soap dispenser pump or instant-hot dispenser that's leaking or no longer pumping. Bottle stays in place under the sink.

entries.title: Touch up exterior trim paint
entries.description: Spot-paint chips, peeling spots, and weather wear on door frames, window casings, and porch posts. Catches the next paint cycle before water damage starts.

entries.title: Replace damaged deck boards
entries.description: Swap warped, split, or rotted deck boards. The handyman matches species and stain so the patch blends with the rest of the deck.

entries.title: Repair or replace mailbox post
entries.description: Reset a leaning mailbox post or install a fresh one. Includes confirming the address numbers are visible from the street.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Install house numbers or address plaque
entries.title: Install house numbers or address plaque
entries.description: Mount new address numbers or a plaque on the house, mailbox, or gate post. Improves visibility for emergency response and deliveries.

entries.title: Replace exterior light fixtures
entries.description: Swap a worn or dated porch, garage, or post light. Includes confirming the wiring is rated for the new fixture's wattage and the gasket seals against weather.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Patch concrete steps and small cracks
entries.title: Patch concrete steps and small cracks
entries.description: Fill chips, spalled corners, and surface cracks in concrete steps, walkways, or patios using a polymer-modified patch.

entries.title: Replace damaged fence pickets
entries.description: Swap rotted, broken, or warped fence pickets without replacing the whole run. Color-match stain so the repair blends.

entries.title: Spot re-stain a deck section
entries.description: Re-stain the highest-wear sections of a deck (rail tops, in front of doors, around the grill) without redoing the whole deck.

entries.title: Replace garage door bottom seal
entries.description: Swap the rubber threshold seal on the bottom of the garage door. Stops drafts, water, and pests from getting under the door.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Lubricate garage door rollers and hinges
entries.title: Lubricate garage door rollers and hinges
entries.description: Apply silicone or lithium-based lubricant to rollers, hinges, and the spring shaft. Quiets the door and extends opener and spring life.
entries.notes: Skip the springs unless you're a pro. High tension and risk of injury.

entries.title: Repair pull-down attic stairs
entries.description: Tighten or replace springs, replace a broken tread, or reset the latch on pull-down attic stairs. Restores safe access to attic storage.

entries.title: Patch chipped epoxy garage floor
entries.description: Spot-patch chipped or peeling epoxy in high-traffic areas of the garage. Re-coat the patch and feather into the surrounding finish.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Install garage shelving or wall-mounted racks
entries.title: Install garage shelving or wall-mounted racks
entries.description: Mount garage shelving units, slatwall, ceiling-mounted overhead racks, or pegboard. Includes confirming wall studs / ceiling joists for safe load.

entries.title: Replace doorbell button (low-voltage)
entries.description: Swap a worn or dated doorbell button at the front door. Easy fix when the button no longer rings consistently.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Install smart smoke and CO detectors
entries.title: Install smart smoke and CO detectors
entries.description: Replace older battery detectors with hardwired or interconnected smart detectors (Nest, First Alert) and confirm the network reports correctly.

entries.title: Replace thermostat batteries
entries.description: Swap the AA or AAA backup batteries in a battery-powered or hybrid-power thermostat. Prevents the mid-cold-snap thermostat blackout.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Place or relocate smart leak sensors
entries.title: Place or relocate smart leak sensors
entries.description: Move existing smart leak sensors to higher-risk spots (under sinks, behind washing machine, near water heater) or add a new round of placements.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Mount and configure a smart camera
entries.title: Mount and configure a smart camera
entries.description: Install a battery- or wired smart camera, secure to the mount, and configure motion zones in the app.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Mount a TV on the wall
entries.title: Mount a TV on the wall
entries.description: Install a wall-mount TV bracket, secure to studs, hang the TV, and route the cables. Includes confirming the bracket is rated for the TV weight.

entries.title: Install floating shelves
entries.description: Hang floating shelves with concealed brackets. Includes confirming the wall stud or anchor type matches the load rating of the shelf.

entries.title: Hang a gallery wall (3+ frames)
entries.description: Lay out, level, and hang a multi-frame arrangement. Includes a paper template pass so you see the layout before any holes go in the wall.

entries.title: Assemble flat-pack furniture
entries.description: Assemble desk, dresser, bookcase, or other knock-down furniture. Includes leveling and confirming all hardware is fully torqued.

entries.title: Install a closet organizer system
entries.description: Install a wire, melamine, or wood closet system. Includes layout planning, anchor placement, and final shelf and rod adjustment.

entries.title: Mount curtain rods and hardware
entries.description: Install curtain or drapery rods, hold-backs, and finials. Includes confirming the bracket is anchored to a stud or rated drywall anchor.

entries.title: Renew snow plowing contract
entries.description: Most snow plow vendors require a signed seasonal contract by mid-fall. Reach out to confirm pricing, set the trigger snowfall depth, and authorize per-storm billing for the season ahead.
entries.notes: Contract typically covers Nov 1 – Apr 1 in the Northeast. Lock it in before October.

entries.templateKey: Mosquito & Tick:Sign up for mosquito and tick season
entries.title: Sign up for mosquito and tick season
entries.description: Most mosquito and tick vendors run seasonal programs. An every-3-week spray schedule from April through October. Sign up in early spring to lock in your spot on their schedule.
entries.notes: Some vendors offer all-natural cedar-oil alternatives if you prefer. Talk to your vendor about program start date so you're covered before tick season peaks.

entries.title: Pruning and crown thinning
entries.description: Selective pruning of mature trees to reduce wind load, eliminate hazardous limbs, and maintain structure. Should be done by an ISA-certified arborist, not a landscaper.
entries.notes: Dormant-season pruning (Dec-Mar) is safest for the trees and cheapest for you.

entries.templateKey: Tree Service:Trim trees away from roof
entries.title: Trim trees away from roof
entries.description: Arborist trims back branches within 10 feet of the roof to prevent storm damage and reduce moss buildup.
entries.notes: Arborist required for large trees

entries.title: Exterior window washing
entries.description: Professional washing of all exterior windows, screens, frame tracks, and sills using purified water systems that leave a streak-free finish without chemical residue. Includes a wipe-down of the frames and removal of any caked pollen, spider webs, and bird debris that builds up in upper corners.
entries.notes: Annual is the right default for most households. Spring after pollen settles is the optimal window. Bump to semi-annual or quarterly for homes that need to stay immaculate (waterfront with salt spray, heavy shade with tree sap, or homes with frequent entertaining). Most premium services include sill and screen cleaning at no extra charge.

entries.title: Annual exterior power washing
entries.description: Soft-wash crew applies a low-pressure cleaning solution and rinses the siding, deck, walkways, and patio. Removes mildew, pollen, and dirt buildup that accumulates over the year and restores curb appeal in one visit. The 'soft-wash' approach (chemistry-driven, low pressure) avoids the wood damage and oxidation streaking that high-pressure washing can cause on siding and decks.
entries.notes: Schedule for late spring after the heaviest pollen settles. That way the cleaning lasts the longest into summer. Hardscape (concrete, stone, pavers) is more forgiving and can take higher pressure if needed. Always confirm with the vendor that they're using soft-wash on siding before they start.

entries.title: Asphalt driveway sealcoat
entries.description: Apply fresh sealcoat to the driveway. Protects against water infiltration, UV damage, and fuel spills.
entries.notes: Apply in early fall while temps are still warm enough for the sealer to cure properly.

entries.title: Annual attic inspection
entries.description: Handyman or attic specialist visually inspects for insulation displacement, pest entry signs, roof-underside leaks, and ventilation issues.
entries.notes: Often included in a fall handyman visit.

entries.title: Annual elevator inspection
entries.description: Certified elevator inspector verifies code compliance: emergency stop, door sensors and interlocks, governor and safety brake, hoist cable wear, machine room ventilation, and updated certificate posting. Required by state law in most jurisdictions for residential elevators. Failing to keep current can void homeowner's insurance for elevator-related claims.
entries.notes: Keep the certificate on file with other estate documents. If your home is on a service contract with an elevator company (Otis, ThyssenKrupp, etc.), the inspection is usually included. But the certificate is something you need to pull and file yourself.

entries.title: Quarterly elevator service
entries.description: Routine service visit covering cable tension and inspection, rail and roller lubrication, door sensor calibration, emergency phone test, and cab leveling check. Catches wear before a small issue becomes a stuck-between-floors call.
entries.notes: Most homes are on a quarterly service contract with the installer or a local specialist. If you've never used the emergency phone, this visit is when to test it. Phone batteries die silently and you don't want to find out you can't call out from inside the cab during the next power blip.

entries.title: Annual cooling unit service
entries.description: Wine cellar specialist services the dedicated cooling unit: cleans evaporator and condenser coils (a clogged coil silently raises cellar temp by 5–10°F), checks refrigerant charge against spec, verifies thermostat calibration to within 1°F, tests humidity controls (ideal: 60–70% RH), and inspects the drain line for the condensate.
entries.notes: Cooling unit failures can ruin a collection overnight. Fine wine starts heat-damaging at 75°F+, and most modern units have no built-in alarm if the compressor fails on a Friday night. This is not a category to skip. Most manufacturer warranties require annual documented service.

entries.title: Annual radon test
entries.description: Place a short-term radon detector kit in the lowest livable level for 2-7 days, then mail it to the lab. Levels above 4 pCi/L require mitigation; 2-4 pCi/L is borderline and worth re-testing. A handyman can handle placement and collection; you don't need a certified radon tester unless you need a real-estate-transaction report.
entries.notes: NH, CT, and much of the surrounding Northeast are in the granite belt, one of the highest radon zones in the country.

entries.templateKey: Air Quality:Service whole-home or basement dehumidifier
entries.title: Service whole-home or basement dehumidifier
entries.description: Clean the filter, wipe the coils, check the drain line for clogs, and verify the humidistat calibration. Catches silent failures that let basements creep above 60% RH and invite mold.
entries.notes: Pair with the spring handyman visit; run a humidity reading after service to confirm.
